| **Data Source** | MET Employability Career Match API |

## Product Question

> Which skills, locations, and role variants give an early-career candidate the strongest entry into Business Intelligence / Data Analyst roles at U.S. securities and investment firms (NAICS 523), and which skills are missing from a current student profile?

## Why This Industry

Securities, commodity contracts, and other financial investment activities (NAICS 523) run continuous reporting, risk, performance-attribution, and client-analytics functions that are staffed by business intelligence and data analyst roles rather than by research scientists. Because investment analytics is shaped by regulatory reporting and legacy data infrastructure, its skill profile differs from the software sector — SQL, data governance, and domain knowledge often matter as much as machine-learning depth. The subsector is also the single largest source of analytics postings within Finance and Insurance in our data source, which makes the scope both coherent and large enough to support a decision-oriented product.

## Scope Revision (Module 2)

Module 1 anchored the project to NAICS 5221, Depository Credit Intermediation. When we pulled the data in Module 2, that code returned **59 postings in total**, of which 13 carried salary information — too thin to support skill-gap and compensation analysis later in the project. We measured the neighbouring industry codes and moved the anchor to **NAICS 523**, which keeps the project inside Finance and Insurance while providing **15,176 postings**, of which **6,199** match our career pathway. The measurement and the filter rule are documented on the Data Preparation page.
